claims.statement: EU F-gas rules require certified undertakings for specified installation and service work and detailed records for equipment subject to leak checks.
Polish owners or managers must report heat pumps as heat sources to CEEB, generally within 14 days of first operation.
Demand hypothesis: installers will pay for a transferable service record if it measurably increases recurring bookings and reduces claim administration.

contrary_evidence: Many small heat pumps fall below F-gas leak-check thresholds or use refrigerants outside the relevant record burden.
OEM portals may already cover parts of warranty and service history.

economics.acquisition_route: Demand hypothesis: prove renewal and booking lift on the family company's installed base, then sell via equipment distributors
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 20000 assets at 10 PLN monthly plus 1.5m PLN booking revenue yields about 3.9m PLN annual revenue; 30% EBITDA at a 5x value could exceed 5m PLN in 4-6 years
economics.founder_time: 12-18 hours weekly; family-business operations provide a bounded test environment
economics.gross_margin_basis: Economics hypothesis: 80% SaaS margin and 65-75% blended margin after payment and support costs
economics.payback: Economics hypothesis: 2500 assets at 10 PLN monthly recover initial capital within 12-15 months before booking margin
economics.pricing: Economics hypothesis: 8-15 PLN per asset monthly plus 6-10% of booked service labor
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual maintenance, leak checks where applicable, repairs, property transfer, and warranty evidence recur over asset life

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Installed-base service history, verified technician performance, and local demand-versus-capacity data
fingerprint.customer: Heat-pump installers, service firms, housing managers, commercial landlords, and equipment owners
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Pilot through the founder's family renewable installer, then OEM distributors, wholesalers, and installer associations
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: White-label asset passport, owner permission controls, service reminders, technician credential checks, and forward-capacity booking
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer pays per active asset monthly and a booking fee when an owner reserves a service slot
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Service is due, a property changes hands, or an installer has idle certified capacity but records and entitlement are fragmented

structure.control_point: Owner-authorized longitudinal asset record linked to the booking and warranty-claim route
structure.critical_dependency: Installers must adopt the workflow and owners must consent; warranty transfer remains subject to each contract

thesis: Installers maintain an owner-permissioned asset record containing commissioning, F-gas work, warranty evidence, and CEEB reminders, then publish forward service slots to property managers. Demand hypothesis: a portable record plus verified capacity will improve maintenance conversion and make installer portfolios more defensible.
title: Heat-Pump Service Passport and Certified-Slot Exchange
